paper_title: DIY-MKG An LLM-Based Polyglot Language Learning System
caption: DIY-MKG reliably expands the vocabulary with low sensitivity to the language and the starting word. For each language, 10 opaque curves represent vocabulary sizes obtained from 10 different starting words, and one solid curve represents the average of the 10 curves. The standard deviations across languages and starting words are small, indicating fairness for all language learners. The diagonal gray line represents the upper-bound of vocabulary size, assuming all words in each iteration have not yet appeared in the vocabulary. While the real expansion rate is lower, the vocabulary does not saturate after 500 iterations. Therefore, DIY-MKG can reliably help the language learner to expand their vocabulary by consistently introducing new words.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the growth of vocabulary size over the number of iterations for three languages—Spanish, Korean, and Japanese—within the DIY-MKG language learning system. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Iterations," ranges from 0 to 500 in increments of 100, representing the progression of the learning process. The y-axis, labeled "Vocabulary Size," spans from 0 to 5000, with major ticks at intervals of 1000, indicating the total number of unique words learned. The plot displays three sets of curves for each language: 10 individual, semi-transparent curves (in blue for Spanish, orange for Korean, and green for Japanese) that represent the vocabulary growth starting from 10 different initial words, and one solid, darker curve of the same color that shows the average of these 10 trajectories. All curves exhibit a steady, approximately linear increase in vocabulary size as iterations progress. For instance, at 500 iterations, the average vocabulary size is around 3200 for Spanish, 3000 for Korean, and 3100 for Japanese. A diagonal gray line, representing the theoretical upper bound where every new word introduced in each iteration is entirely novel, is also included; it reaches a vocabulary size of 5000 at 500 iterations. The actual vocabulary growth curves remain below this upper bound but show no sign of saturation, indicating consistent word acquisition. The small spread between the individual curves and the close proximity of the average curves to the upper bound suggest low sensitivity to the starting word and consistent performance across languages.
